course_name_original: Modern systems of light sources supply and control
course_name_en: Modern systems of light sources supply and control

learning_outcomes.text: Knows the basics of lighting technology and photometry.
Knows the construction and operation of incandescent, fluorescent, high-pressure discharge lamps and LED diodes.
Knows the construction of power supply systems for LED lamps, fluorescent lamps, discharge lamps and incandescent lamps.
Knows the regulation methods for power supply systems of LED lamps, fluorescent lamps, discharge lamps and incandescent lamps.
Knows the basic problems of lighting control.
Is familiar with the current state and latest development trends of light sources, power electronic supply systems and their control systems.
Knows the problems of environmental hazards of materials used for the construction of artificial light sources and hazards related to the use of artificial light sources.
Is familiar with the possibilities of using computer tools to support lighting design.
Can reproduce circuit models of simple power supply systems for artificial light sources.
Can analyze the operation and perform simulations of simple electronic and power electronic systems for supplying artificial light sources.
Can analyze and simulate simple automatic control systems for converters supplying artificial light sources to assess their operation in steady and dynamic states.
Ability to use selected computer tools to support the design of lighting systems.
Understands the need for continuous learning related to rapid changes in lighting technology.

Is aware of the importance and understands the non-technical aspects and consequences of an electrical engineer's activity, including its impact on the environment, and the related responsibility for decisions made.

syllabus_topics: Physical basics of lighting technology and photometry and parameters characterizing light sources.
Classification of light sources, basic physical and application properties of lamps.
Diode light sources: basics of LED technology, power electronic supply systems, application problems and LED lamps.
Low-pressure and high-pressure discharge lamps: construction and parameters of lamps, conventional and power electronic supply systems and control aspects.
Use of incandescent light sources in modern lighting technology.
Issues of energy efficiency of lighting systems.
Issues related to the negative impact of lamps and their recycling.
Control and management of complex lighting systems.
Analysis of lighting effects and electrical signals in exemplary applications of artificial light source power supply.
Analysis of control in LED light source power supply systems.
Use of selected computer tools to support the design of lighting systems.
Power electronic systems for powering LED light sources.
Power electronic systems for powering fluorescent lamps and lamp power regulation.
Power electronic systems for powering discharge lamps and lamp power regulation.
assessment_rules: Lectures: Students participate in classes, learning subsequent teaching content according to the course syllabus. Students should ask questions and clarify doubts on an ongoing basis. Audiovisual recording of the lecture requires the consent of the instructor. Laboratory classes: Students perform laboratory exercises according to the materials provided by the instructor. The student is obliged to prepare for the exercise being performed, which may be verified by an oral or written colloquium. Passing the classes is based on presenting a solution to the problem. Passing the module is possible after passing all laboratory classes.
